Welcome to Heronsgate Primary School
As a school, we look forward to sharing this period of your child’s life with you. We believe that a child’s primary education is fundamental to their success in life and that it should be a special time for your child.
We hope Heronsgate provides memories and friendships they will cherish for the rest of their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Values and Aims — Heronsgate Primary School
pageCache.text:
Values and Aims
Our Vision Statement
We discover and realise the genius in everyone
We learn about and respect the people with whom we share our world
We constantly develop and acquire the skills needed to achieve personal success
We build up our confidence in ourselves
We learn to treat and respect others the way we like to be treated
Our Aims
To create a stimulating environment which reflects our values and promotes a sense of self-worth and community.
To build strong collaborative partnerships with families and the local community.
To provide a broad, balanced and creative curriculum that combines excellence in teaching with enjoyment of learning.
To recognise and plan for a range of learning styles and interests, to ensure all children have equal access to the curriculum enabling them to reach their full potential.
To promote life-long learning through high quality continual professional development for all staff and by developing a learning culture throughout the school.
To promote social, cultural, moral and spiritual development, supporting pupils and staff to become confident and responsible members of society.
To establish an atmosphere in which each child has a positive self-image and where individual achievements are valued by all.
To include all members of the school community in the process of school improvement and self evaluation.
Values-Based Education
Heronsgate provides a Values-based curriculum. This means that we promote and teach a set of values to our pupils that will ensure they develop the skills to be good citizens in the future. We support our curriculum with a set of principles (values) that are woven into teaching and learning in order to develop improved social and emotional skills that will positively affect behaviour.
“Why do we behave the way we do? What is it that drives us to give to charity or to help children to develop as happy, stable people? It is our values that determine our thinking and our behaviour. They are the principles, standards or life stances that act as guides to our behaviour. They are our beliefs about what is worthwhile, the ideals for which we strive. They are the standards by which particular beliefs and actions are judged to be good or desirable. They help us make decisions and evaluate the actions of others.”
(Dr Neil Hawkes – An International Educational Consultant who has been working with our teachers.)
There are 6 values that we consider to be universal:
Each month we lead a special values assembly, teachers also explicitly teach the ‘Value of the Month’ in PSHCE lessons. Wherever possible the value of the month is taught in other areas of the curriculum. Most importantly, adults in the school ensure that we are role-models for each of the values.
Teaching children values improves pupils’ self-esteem, improves their behaviour and raises standards of learning even higher.

Welcome
We would like to welcome you to Heronsgate Primary School.
Heronsgate is a friendly, hardworking school set in large attractive grounds across two sites, one in West Thamesmead and the other at Burrage Grove in Woolwich.
At our Thamesmead Campus we have a morning nursery class and two/three classes in each year group from Year 1 to Year 6.Our Royal Arsenal Campus is a smaller site with one class in each year group from Reception to Year 6.
We are passionate about children achieving their absolute best in all areas of the curriculum and in developing a true love of learning. Our vision is encapsulated by our core values of responsibility, respect, resilience, kindness, honesty and co-operation.
If you have any questions about our school, please contact the school office.
Stephen Harris (Executive Headteacher)Shahnaz Ahmed (Headteacher)

What others say about us
Parent of Year 6 children
As our two daughters come to the end of their time at Heronsgate Primary School after two very special years, I wanted to take a moment to express our heartfelt thanks to everyone who has been part of their journey.
They have loved Heronsgate Primary School so much. To them, it has felt like a second home, and that is a reflection of the wonderful teachers, support staff and everyone who makes the school such a special place. They have made happy memories, built friendships, learned so much and grown in confidence during their time here.
We are incredibly grateful to every member of the Heronsgate team who has played a part in our daughters' lives, whether directly in the classroom or behind the scenes. Your patience, kindness, encouragement and dedication will always be remembered by our family.
Although they are moving on to their next chapter, Heronsgate will always hold a very special place in our hearts. Thank you for making these two years so memorable and for caring for our daughters as if they were your own.
Grandparent of Year 6 child
As my grandson comes to the end of his primary school journey and prepares to start secondary school, I wanted to take a moment to thank you all for everything you have done for him over the years.Your kindness, patience, encouragement, and dedication have helped him grow not only academically but also into a confident, caring, and respectful young person. We are so grateful for the support and opportunities you have given him, and we know he will carry many happy memories of his time at your school.I'd also like to include a few words from him:"Thank you to all my teachers and everyone at school for helping me learn and grow. I've made lots of great memories and wonderful friends that I'll never forget. Thank you for always encouraging me and believing in me. I'm excited to start secondary school, but I'll always remember my time here and everyone who made it so special."Please accept our sincere thanks for everything you have done. We wish the school, staff, and pupils every success for the future.

Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast Club
Heronsgate Breakfast Club runs from Monday to Friday from 7:30am to 8:50am when the children are taken to their class lines ready for the start of school. This club runs at both Thamesmead and Royal Arsenal campuses.
Breakfast Club is offered to children in Reception to Year 6. During the session, the children are given a healthy breakfast and there are a range of stimulating activities for them to do, including games, art activities and reading. These activities are supervised by members of Heronsgate School staff.
If you wish to book your child in to Breakfast Club, please do so via ParentPay by 8am on the day at the latest.There are a limited number of spaces so booking in advance is essential.There is a charge of £5 per session.
We aim to promote an enjoyable and healthy breakfast which will last the children through to lunchtime.
Everyday the children will get a choice of:
Toast with jam or marmite
A selection of cereals
After School Club
Sportacus runs an After School Club daily from 3:30pm - 6pm.
Please visit their website at https://www.sportacus.co.uk/wrap-around for more details.

Extra-curricular clubs
Clubs at Heronsgate
Every half-term we offer a selection of clubs to our children across both campuses. Some of these are run in-house, others by external companies.
A letter will go out to parents regularly with full details of the clubs on offer, dates and the cost. All club places must be booked via ParentPay.
This half-term, children are taking part in the following clubs:

Governors
Role of Governors at our school
The government expects governing bodies to have a strong focus on three core strategic functions:
Ensuring clarity of vision, ethos and strategic direction
Holding the Headteacher to account for the educational performance of the school and its pupils and the performance management of staff
Overseeing the financial performance of the school and making sure its money is well spent.(Governance Handbook – Department for Education, 2025)
The governing body focuses its time and energy on school improvement. Governors work collectively to support and strengthen the leadership of the Executive Headteacher and challenge where necessary. Governors play a strategic role; the Executive Headteacher is responsible for the routine running of the school.

Curriculum
At Heronsgate Primary we are committed to a broad, balanced and inclusive curriculum which enthuses and motivates learners, extending and enriching their knowledge and understanding of the world we live in- so they are able to make a valuable contribution as they grow.
Our curriculum framework recognises that children learn best when they are actively engaged, can make links in their learning and are given opportunities to talk about and apply their learning in different contexts. As such our curriculum, in addition to meeting all statutory requirements and challenge, is contextualised and learning is enriched through the arts and visits to places of interest.
Our ‘Heronsgate Charter for Secondary Ready’ not only outlines the high academic performance we expect our children to have achieved but an array of opportunities they will have had such as, for example, learning a musical instrument or a visit to the theatre. This we hope will give them the confidence, motivation and skills needed to flourish in secondary school and beyond.

Design and Technology
Please see our SEND Policy and Report for information on how our curriculum is accessible. Please contact us to find out more about the curriculum at Heronsgate Primary School.
Phonics
We use the ‘Little Wandle Letters and Sounds’ phonics programme, starting in Reception and continuing into Key Stage 1. Reception begin by learning the single letter sounds and then learn to blend these sounds into words (e.g. ‘h-a-t’ becomes hat). Children are then taught to segment sounds and blend them together into words in order that they can read and write efficiently. Children also learn to read and write ‘tricky’ words, which have an unusual spelling and cannot be sounded out fully. In Year 1 children learn the alternative spellings for different sounds. Phonics is taught every day, with the children learning a new sound and revising sounds already taught. Some children will receive additional phonics support if we feel that this will be of benefit.
At the end of Year 1, children are assessed through the national phonics screening check. For any children who need it, phonics sessions continue in Year 2, and beyond if necessary, until they are fluent readers. Once children can read fluently, reading then progresses from learning to read, to reading to learn.
The school uses the ‘Big Cat for Little Wandle’ decodable reading books. Children read these books with an adult in school, developing their ability to decode, read with expression and understand the book. They then take this book home to read aloud and ‘show off’ their skills to an adult. Alongside this they take home a sharing book to enjoy with an adult. We believe that children need exposure to a variety of reading material to appeal to their different interests.
At the early stages of reading development, the children initially use books without text and progress to books that are directly linked to the phonics sounds that they are learning. Children progress through the reading scheme at their own pace; they do not need to read a certain number of books in each stage before moving on to the next level. Alongside ‘decoding’ the words (using their phonics to read the words), we stress the importance of chatting and asking questions about what they are reading to ensure the children understand what they have read. We ask that parents and anyone hearing children read always talk about the book with them and complete their ‘Reading Champions’ record.
Please click here for further parent information and videos, to enable you to support your child with phonics – https://www.littlewandlelettersandsounds.org.uk/resources/for-parents.
Reading Champions Home/School Record
Children are encouraged to read at home as frequently as possible and parents and carers are asked to record their reading in the child’s Reading Champions Book. This really makes a huge difference to a child’s reading skills! As a school, we very much appreciate all families who support reading and hear children read at home – we know your time is precious, but it is a vital part of every child’s education. As well as hearing children read, it is important that adults chat with children about their book – the characters, what they are doing and what might happen next!
Follow the link for more information on how to support your child’s reading at home.

Inclusion and Special Educational Needs (SEN)
We are an inclusive school.
Our teaching staff are pro-active in planning to meet the learning needs of pupils in their class. We use a range of approaches including adapting lessons and offering additional sessions to support children.
More information about our approach can be found in our SEN policy and Annual Report. This can be found on our policies page.
If parents would like to talk to a member of our staff about SEN needs then they should contact their class teacher.
If parents would like to talk to our SENDCos (Carly Bashford and Caroline Dalton-Hutchinson) then they should contact the office by phone or email (see details at the bottom of the page).
Local Authority offer for Special Educational Needs
The Local Authority offer for Special Educational Needs is a powerful resource that gives parents useful information about different support available within our local area.
This includes links to support groups, activities and other resources.
It can be accessed here: Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Local Offer | Greenwich Community Directory
Greenwich SENDIASS provide free all-year round Special Educational Needs and Disability information; advice and support service (SENDIASS) for Young People, children and Parents aged 0 to 25.
School Acronyms and Abbreviations
Click here for a link to some useful explanations to the acronyms and abbreviations used in schools.Click here for a link to a glossary of terms relating to Special Educational Needs and Disabilities.

IT & Computing
Our Vision
In a world where technology plays a key role in all of our lives, we want to equip children to confidently and creatively learn using technology.
At Heronsgate, our vision is to:
Provide staff and all children with safe, sufficient, high quality and up-to-date IT resources for teaching and learning
Use technology as a tool for learning, transforming what is possible in the classroom
Enable children to access home learning through the effective use of technology
Teach children how to keep themselves safe whilst using the Internet
Equip every child to be makers with digital technology rather than just consumers
Deepen children’s learning through using technology as a creative tool and thus raising attainment across the curriculum
Overcome barriers to learning through using technology
Build staff confidence, pedagogy and subject knowledge so they can continue to be leaders of technology in the classroom
Engage with parents and the wider community so they feel empowered to use technology to support learning and keep their children safe online
iPad Toolkit
We believe that technology can help with learning by facilitating:
Engaging Experiences – learning by doing helps children remember and understand. iPad engages learners with memorable experiences.
Creative Collaboration – creating something new helps children apply their learning. iPad facilitates learners working together on tasks.
Thoughtful Reflection – evaluating and analysing helps children develop their thinking. Using iPad provides tools for learners to reflect on their learning.
Parent E-Safety Resources
Follow this link to the London Grid for Learning for a range of resources for parents on how to keep children safe online.
Childnet also has some useful resources for parents.

pageCache.pageTitle: Super Small Scientists — Heronsgate Primary School
pageCache.text:
Super Small Scientists
Pupils have demonstrated progression in their scientific competencies this term, specifically through the application of observational techniques and the accurate recording of data.
Cause and Effect - EYFS
In the nursery (EYFS) setting, the sensory exploration of dry and wet playdough seen in the image is crucial for developing early scientific skills. As children predict what might happen when they add water to the light blue, crumbly mixture on the black tray, they are beginning to think like little scientists. This hands-on process allows them to observe first-hand the transformation of materials and directly understand cause and effect as they see their guesses come to life through play
Mini-Monster Hunters - KS1
Year 2 pupils have been investigating animals and their habitats, specifically focusing on the playground's microhabitats. During a practical minibeast hunt, the children identified and recorded the various species inhabiting different environmental niches. To organise their findings, the children collated their data into tables, which were then presented and shared during a class-wide review. The session concluded with a comparative discussion regarding the impact of environmental variables, exploring how a change in a single factor would alter the suitability of a habitat.
Heating Up Cool Ideas - LKS2
This work demonstrates a Year 4 pupil’s application of melting point theory within the "Changing State" unit. The student utilized their understanding of thermal properties to design a controlled scientific inquiry determining the relative melting rates of various food substances. To document the process and results, the pupil captured video observations and organized the resulting data into a results table. This approach allowed for a clear comparison of how different materials respond to consistent heat sources.
A Beak Into Evolution
Year 6 pupils have been studying the mechanisms of natural selection through a practical investigation The students simulated how variations in beak shapes affect a bird's ability to feed and survive within a specific environment .Through this inquiry, the children explored the correlation between physical traits and survival rates. The study concluded with a discussion on extinction, examining how species that fail to naturally evolve, are unable to compete when their environment or food sources change.
Nest of Discoveries
Believing in Better

pageCache.pageTitle: Nest of Discoveries — Heronsgate Primary School
pageCache.text:
Nest of Discoveries
Numbers Stick with Dice, and Bricks - EYFS
In the Nest EYFS provision children have been learning about place value using concrete objects such as a dice, large numbers and foam bricks.
Hard Facts, Soft Beads - KS1
In the Nest provision, our KS1 children have been learning about states of matter using water beads and exploring how they change from hard to soft.
Pulling Together In Science - LKS2
The lower KS2 children in the Nest provision have been learning about forces using magnets. They have been investigating what objects are magnetic in their environment. They were also using magnets to sort non mental and metal objects.
Reaching New Heights - UKS2
The upper KS2 children are learning about height and exploring using tape measures to measure each other and compare heights.

pageCache.pageTitle: Believing in Better — Heronsgate Primary School
pageCache.text:
Believing in Better
Across the school in Spring 1 children explored commitment to God through different faiths and how someone’s actions exemplifies their understanding of how God wants them to treat the world. Through reflection children were able to make links to their own faith or understanding of the world.
Green Thumbs, Good Years - EYFS
In Reception, the children discussed New Year's resolutions. They reflected upon what commitments they would like to make in looking after nature in their outside areas.
Faith in a Better Future - KS1
In Year 1, the children thought about a Christian’s commitment to God and his creation. They reflected upon whether, in their opinion, god would be happy or unhappy with the way humans are looking after his creation. The children used iPads to support their learning by leaving a voice note explaining their thoughts/ideas.
Shared Core Values - LKS2
In Year 3, the children explored how three different faiths understand how the world came into being and their commitment in looking after the world that was created by God. After discussing the similarities and difference they reflected upon their own attitudes to life, living things and the world.
Pillars of Commitment - UKS2
In Year 5, the children reflected upon their learning of the five pillars of Islam and discussed which pillar they considered to show a Muslim’s greatest commitment to Allah. We also presented our learning to parents and the school during both KS1 and KS2 during the Ramadan period.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE and Sports Premium — Heronsgate Primary School
pageCache.text:
PE and Sports Premium
Physical activity is an important part of our curriculum at Heronsgate Primary School. We want our children to lead healthy, active lives and to have a positive attitude towards exercise through both individual activities and team sports.Part of our funding for our provision of Physical Education (PE) comes from the Sports Premium grant. The Department for Education pays this grant annually.
Information about our strategy for using this funding is below.
Heronsgate Sports Premium Strategy 2025-2026

School Dinners
We are proud to work with Chartwells Schools for your children’s school dinners. Chartwells believe that the key to fuelling young minds comes from understanding both what they need and what they enjoy, which is why they develop nutritious and delicious food that pupils love, whilst helping to ensure a healthy body and mind.
Their passionate culinary experts work closely with us to ensure every child receives healthy food, perfectly suited to meet their needs and dietary requirements.
Chartwells’s Food Super Heroes make food education fun, whatever the age, and their tasty theme days encourage children to make the most of their school meal.
To find out more about Chartwells, visit their website or contact the school catering team.
If your child has a food allergy or intolerance and you would like to discuss this, please the Chartwells medical diet nutrition team directly via this email address.
School Meal Pricing
All children are able to have a hot meal daily, with children in EYFS to Year 2 eligible for a universal free school meal.
For children in Years 3 to 6, meals are also free under the Mayor of London’s free school meal programme. Please note, meal choices should be made half termly.
London Grid for Learning have a free tool that parents can use to check if their child is eligible for Free School Meals. You can access this via https://pps.lgfl.org.uk/.
To apply for Free School Meals, please visit the Royal Greenwich website.
Dinner Menu
Every day, you can be assured that a school meal will offer:
• At least two portions of fruit and vegetables
• Dairy food items rich in calcium for strong bones and teeth
• Starchy carbohydrates to provide energy
• A protein source to support the body’s growth and repair
Packed Lunch
If your child does not like hot (healthy) school dinners, they can opt to bring a packed lunch.
Please ensure that packed lunches are brought into school in a secure container labelled with your child’s name. They should contain no high sugar foods, fizzy drinks or foods which will not stay fresh without refrigeration. We ask you do not send in foods containing nuts.Please see our Healthy Schools letter for ideas of what to pack in your child’s lunch.
